The concept of ray casting for volume rendering originated in the early 1990s as a direct solution to the visualization of 3D scalar fields without intermediate surface extraction.

The method has become a standard technique in scientific visualization, medical imaging, and geosciences, evolving from CPU-based implementations to highly optimized GPU shaders and distributed parallel systems.
